analysis:
The PR is a CI/release toolchain bump to Xcode 27.2 (SDK 27.2, Swift 6.4.2) plus docs and tests. Examined: provider-release-cache.yml (new DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN set to 'qualification' for pull_request and 'release' otherwise, via a trusted github.event_name expression, with no injection), provider-signing-validation.yml (the inline SDK 27.0 check is replaced by tooling/scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh in release mode, invoked from the trusted tooling checkout, not the candidate), release-provider.yml (workflow-level env release at head 112-114, validation assertion build_sdk_version=='27.2' at head 1444), scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py:82 (hardcoded 27.2), mise.toml, the changelog, build.md, test.md and provider-release.md. The test script scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py asserts fail-closed behavior (no GITHUB_ENV written on refusal, unknown mode exits 2, anchored Swift version match, explicit DEVELOPER_DIR as sole candidate). No change touches provider runtime, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest or cache code, so TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013 and T-041 are unaffected. Signing steps (hardened runtime, entitlements, get-task-allow absence, final-bytes SDK check, keychain deletion) are unchanged. Release publication still derives the CDHash and binary hash from the final signed bytes (A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054). No secrets are added, and no permissions or triggers change.

Unverified contracts, which I record as questions rather than findings. (1) The script body (prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh) and the swift wrapper were not supplied as numbered source. Whether release mode fails closed on non-27.2 is therefore only evidenced through the tests and docs. (2) Qualification is the default mode. Any release or signing job that does not set release could accept SDK 27.0, though the visible release workflows set it. (3) identity.py hardcodes build_sdk_version=27.2 rather than deriving it from the artifact, so a resumed pre-bump unsigned artifact could be mislabeled unless downstream verification checks the real linked SDK; the changelog states resume signs only a 27.2-linked build, but that check is not shown. (4) Omitted replay units limit coverage.
